### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**10** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/ai/knowledge-rag.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/architecture.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/events.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via handleAIRequest (symbol, a top-level function))_
- `content/docs/plugins/anatomy.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/index.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via ObjectKernel (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **231** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **166** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **166**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **107** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **55** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 758c0b455b5b8c2b20b02e373eb4f857959a0a1b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c8bea5a9252011384e2aabd3ea3b696594455c9f` — the merge of head `ae41bcd980ecf70a63d27434c6fcf81565aa7ff3` into base `758c0b455b5b8c2b20b02e373eb4f857959a0a1b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c8bea5a9252011384e2aabd3ea3b696594455c9f && git checkout c8bea5a9252011384e2aabd3ea3b696594455c9f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 758c0b455b5b8c2b20b02e373eb4f857959a0a1b ae41bcd980ecf70a63d27434c6fcf81565aa7ff3 && git checkout -B drift-repro 758c0b455b5b8c2b20b02e373eb4f857959a0a1b && git merge --no-ff ae41bcd980ecf70a63d27434c6fcf81565aa7ff3

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 758c0b455b5b8c2b20b02e373eb4f857959a0a1b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 758c0b455b5b8c2b20b02e373eb4f857959a0a1b` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位 ACCEPT · head `ae41bcd980ecf70a63d27434c6fcf81565aa7ff3`

#31905 (cloud#3582 install run). `Clause-②: yes (widening)` / `Metadata-protocol: none`. The paths give no review face, so the seat reviewed it at TIER_DEFAULT. Not governed. The seat patched the PR body to this head (the seat-post path).

- **The signal.** `hasBootPhaseSettled('kernel:ready')` is a read-only public method on `ObjectKernel` and `LiteKernel`, a widening named in the changeset. It latches after `trigger('kernel:ready')` returns, so every `start()` and every ready handler has run, and it answers only while the state is `running`. Every other phase name answers false, and so do withheld boot-phase hooks and a stopped kernel. The dispatcher reads it duck-typed off the same request kernel `getRegisteredAiRoutes` reads.
- **The off arm.** `aiUnavailable()` is the unserveable exit's answer, moved verbatim (`GET /ai/agents` → 200 `{ agents: [] }`, everything else → `capabilityUnavailable`). The `!routes` exit keeps the #7653 anonymous gate first. It answers "off" only when the request kernel is past ready, and keeps the boot-race 503 in every other case.
- **The seat's should-fix (round 1), done.** `DomainHandlerDeps` is exported from the runtime root, so `isRequestKernelReady?` is now OPTIONAL and read as `?.(context) === true`. An outside implementation still compiles and keeps the 503. This is pinned (E CONTROL, a deps without the seam), and ablation A7 turns it red.
- **Accepted as-is:** the reused 501 sentence names the package as absent, which is slightly off on an unlicensed Enterprise image, and the Console reads only `/ai/agents`. The seam name is `isRequestKernelReady`.
- **Out of scope, carrier cloud:** discovery still reports `services.ai` `handlerReady: true` on such an install. The root fix is the producer carrying the ADR-0076 D12 degraded marker, and the seat notifies the cloud mailbox on landing.
- **Evidence:** the base leg has 6 red (503), and the ablations A1–A7 were each red, then restored. Core 3254, runtime 9205 / 19 skipped, typecheck and eslint 0. dispatch-gates 71/71 reconciled on ae41bcd9. No new route, so the dogfood package is not owed.

Landing: once CI is all green, check K, then relay `pr_ready` + `automerge_enable`.
